How to Submit Public Comment:
Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of the following
methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit it to the City
Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes per person per item. At the
Mayor’ s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to allow all speakers to address the City Council.

Electronic submission of Public Comment is also available via the City’s website as noted below.
Public Comment submitted electronically will be read into the record. Words that would disrupt the
meeting, including profanity, obscenity, and discriminatory language, will not be read. Your
comments must be received by 5:00 P.M. on meeting day.

Website: Please submit your comments using the online public comment form at Public Comment.

Watch the Meeting Online
Live broadcasts of the meetings are available using the following link: City Council Meeting Videos

Spectrum cable: Live streaming on Channel 3, Public Access Channel.

   MINUTES OF TUESDAY, OCTOBER 24, 2023
  MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL
  HUMAN EQUITY, ACCESS, AND RELATIONS (HEAR) COMMISSION

CALL TO ORDER

Chair Jennings-Nuñez called the regular meeting of the HEAR Commission to order at 6:32 p.m.
on Tuesday, October 24, 2023, in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South Mission Drive, San
Gabriel, California, 91776.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Commissioner Herrera-Avila.

ROLL CALL

Commissioners Present:  Michelle Brenhaug, Viki Goto, Riaz (Rick) Khan, and Chasity
  Jennings-Nuñez

Commissioners Absent:  Eric Chen, George Herrera-Avila, and Cathie Chavez-Morris

Youth Ambassadors:  Aaron Situ (Kelly Munoz Rios was absent)

ANNOUNCEMENTS

Matthew Morales-Stevens, Community Services Manager, provided information for the public on
how to submit comments, and how to request meeting agendas. If you wish to address the HEAR
Commission, e-mail all public comments to HEARCommission@sgch.org.

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  The agenda order was approved.

  2. PUBLIC COMMENT

HEAR COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  OCTOBER 24, 2023
   None.

  3. ACTION ITEMS

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  Chair Jennings-Nuñez provided a minor edit to the minutes.

  A motion was made by Commissioner Brenhaug and seconded by Commissioner
  Khan to approve the amended minutes from September 26, 2023.

  Motion approved as presented by a vote of 4-0-0-3 as follows:
  Ayes: Brenhaug, Goto, Khan, Jennings-Nuñez
  Nays: None
  Abstain: None
  Absent: Chen, Chavez-Morris, Herrera-Avila, Khan

  Public Comment: None

  4. DISCUSSION ITEMS

  A. DISCUSSION OF THE APPROVED 2023 ANNUAL WORKPLAN
  Presented by Chair Jennings-Nuñez.

  The Commission would like to host an informal meeting with Police Chief Elizalde
  regarding data collection.

  Public Comment: None

  B. 2023 MENTAL WELLNESS EXPO REVIEW
  Presented by Chair Jennings-Nuñez.

  The Commission said the event was better organized but was disappointed with
  the turnout. They found the workshops and booths to be engaging but felt that
  most people mostly stayed for the raffles. The Commissioners thanked the
  department staff for all their help.

  Public Comment: None

  C. 2024 ANNUAL WORKPLAN PREPARATION
  Presented by Chair Jennings-Nuñez.

  The commission suggested focusing on a specific area, such as access and
  inclusion. They discussed adding and removing items from their work plan for the

HEAR COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  OCTOBER 24, 2023
   next year. Some of these changes included adding a youth-led project about the
  climate crisis and removing the Mental Wellness Expo. Commissioners requested
  to work with staff and be included in vetting mental health programs and
  initiatives that will be presented to the city council.

  Public Comment: None

  D. ALL ARE WELCOME PROGRAM & PRIDE TOUR DISCUSSION
  Presented by Manager Morales-Stevens

  The commission held a discussion regarding deadlines, they would like
  participating businesses to be signed up by June. The first group will serve as a
  pilot group.

  A motion was made by Chair Jennings-Nuñez and seconded by Vice Chair Goto
  to move forward with the All Are Welcome Program with recommended changes,
  budget, and presentation to the city council.

  Motion approved as presented by a vote of 4-0-0-3 as follows:
  Ayes: Brenhaug, Goto, Khan, Jennings-Nuñez
  Nays: None
  Abstain: None
  Absent: Chen, Chavez-Morris, Herrera-Avila, Khan

  Another motion was made by Chair Jennings-Nuñez and seconded by
  Commissioner Brenhaug to participate in the Pride Tour and that the city council
  identify a liaison to the SGV LGBTQ committee for the tour.

  Motion approved as presented by a vote of 4-0-0-3 as follows:
  Ayes: Brenhaug, Goto, Khan, Jennings-Nuñez
  Nays: None
  Abstain: None
  Absent: Chen, Chavez-Morris, Herrera-Avila, Khan

  Public Comment: None

  5. COMMISSION REPORTS

  Vice Chair Goto shared that the Center for the Preservation of Democracy and the
  Smithsonian Institution Traveling Exhibition Service will be hosting an exhibit titled “The
  Bias Inside Us” from November 18 to January 28. She also mentioned that the Public
  Utilities Commission will be holding virtual public hearings regarding the Broadband
  Equity Access and Deployment (BEAD) Program on November 8. Additionally, Vice Chair
  Goto shared information regarding accessible hiking trails.

HEAR COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  OCTOBER 24, 2023
   Chair Jennings-Nuñez highlighted the ending of Hispanic Heritage Month, the beginning
  of Native American Heritage Month, and the city’s Dia De Los Muertos Celebration. There
  will also be a Kiwanis Club happy hour event at Ogopogo, Chair Jennings-Nuñez invites
  the community to attend.

  Commission Khan attended two events, the La Casa Fundraiser and Kiwanis Club meeting
  where he met the new police chief. He mentioned there will be a fundraiser held by the
  police department on Thursday, October 26.

  Youth Ambassador Situ attended a voter pre-registration workshop and is currently
  working on starting a drive at his school.

  STAFF COMMENTS
  Manager Morales-Stevens shared information regarding the Veteran’s Day Luncheon on
  November 9 and the Veteran’s Day Ceremony on November 10.

  6. ADJOURNMENT

  Chair Jennings-Nuñez adjourned the meeting at 8:14 p.m.

  The next regular meeting is scheduled in person for Tuesday, November 28, 2023, at 6:30
  p.m.

DATE:  May 23, 2023

TO:  HEAR Commission

FROM:  Matthew Morales-Stevens, Community Services Manager

SUBJECT:  HEAR Commission 2023 Approved Annual Workplan

SUMMARY
This is the Annual Workplan developed by the Human Equity, Access and Relations
Commission and is intended for the 2023 calendar year. The 2023 Annual Workplan was
approved by the City Council during the April 18, 2023 Council meeting.

Purpose of the Commission
The purpose of the HEAR Commission is to advance and advocate for equity, access,
diversity, social justice, safety, mutual appreciation, increased cultural competency,
positive inter-group relations and respect for all members of the San Gabriel community.

Scope of the Commission
The HEAR Commission serves as an advisory body to the City Council and reports directly
to the City Council to assess and recommend policies, procedures and activities in the City
government to advance the Commission’s purpose. It is not intended for the HEAR
Commission to be a quasi-judicial body, an oversight board, nor a body whose primary
function is to receive or investigate individual incidents or complaints. The HEAR
Commission may request and obtain information with respect to individual incidents or
complaints, but only to the extent necessary to make policy, procedure or activity
recommendations to the City Council.

Purpose of the Annual Workplan
The Annual Workplan is intended to guide the work of the HEAR Commission and outline
the areas of focus for the remainder of 2023. It includes proposed programs and projects
that will be implemented and completed throughout the year, some of which may extend
beyond 2023. Some of the items have carried over from the 2022 workplan.
   HEAR Commission 2023 Approved Annual Workplan
  May 23, 2023
  Page 2

APPROVED 2023 WORKPLAN
The 2023 Workplan sets forth seven priority areas that the HEAR Commission has
identified as key areas of interest in furthering its purpose. The following list of ideas,
programs and activities are not intended to be exhaustive or to limit the action items the
Commission can explore.

  1. Equity Training and Inequities in City Policies (Meets the Goals and Purpose of the
  Commission for Equity)
  a. Recommend that all City staff members be required to participate in
  implicit-bias training.

  2. Community Engagement (Meets the Goals and Purpose of the Commission for
  Diversity, Mutual Appreciation and Increased Cultural Competency)
  a. Develop and implement programs and events, possibly in partnership with
  the Community Services Commission and Department, that engage and
  educate the community to promote the goals of the HEAR Commission
  i. Examples include: a culturally-diverse movie night, continue the SG
  Mental Wellness Expo and continue further work in support of the
  indigenous population within San Gabriel
  1. The Commission is requesting that $2,500 is budgeted for the
  Mental Wellness Expo in Fiscal Year 2023-2024. This will
  enable the Commission to continue and expand the event in
  2023 without reliance on third-party funding.
  b. Ensure the City continues to recognize Native American Heritage Month and
  Black History Month, at a minimum by proclamation, with the hopes of
  expansion.
  c. Guest speaker(s)/ educational program(s) during the regular Commission
  meetings (one per month) which relate to the scope of the Commission.
  i. Examples include: Bystander Training, anti-bias training, cultural
  diversity,  mental-health  awareness,  low-income  housing,
  homelessness and other relevant topics.
  ii. Recommend that the City continues with an annual or bi-annual
  implicit-bias training.
  d. Develop and implement programs and activities that make sustainable
  practices accessible to everyone to reduce impacts of climate change on low
  and moderate-income communities.
  e. Work with staff to develop a safe zone/space campaign geared toward
  creating offices, business and public spaces that can be easily identified as
  safe spaces for minority populations, specifically the LGBTQ+ population.
   HEAR Commission 2023 Approved Annual Workplan
  May 23, 2023
  Page 3

  f. Create and assign an active community member award from the HEAR
  Commission.
  g. Recommend to City Council that the City implement a multicultural event/
  celebration that could be done in conjunction with the City’s birthday
  celebration.

3. Youth Engagement (Meets the Goals and Purpose of the Commission for Diversity
  and Access)
  a. Add two youth liaisons to the current HEAR Commission to enable the youth
  voice to be heard within the community. Each representative would be
  chosen through an application process and selected by the Commission.
  b. Promote and/ or develop youth internships opportunities, including but not
  limited to a Social Media internship.

4. Community Information (Meets the Goals and Purpose of the Commission for
  Access)
  a. Identify ways in which the City can provide additional social services to the
  community and determine/specify what those services would be.
  i. Connect people with resources on a more local level- care
  coordination, which addresses how people can receive various
  services from the fewest locations possible thereby allowing for
  easier access to services.
  ii. Make resources available to economically-disadvantaged youth.
  b. Implement a resource page on the City website on various topics relating to
  the scope of the Commission.
  c. Implement a fraud/cybersecurity seminar, potentially through the San
  Gabriel Police Department.

5. Accessibility (Meets the Goals and Purpose of the Commission for Access)
  a. Determine various forms of outreach specifically for persons whose primary
  language is not English to ensure meetings and activities are accessible.

6. Partnerships (Meets the Goals and Purpose of the Commission for Increased cultural
  competence and positive inter-group relations)
  a. Seek partnerships with various agencies to address the purpose of the
  Commission.
  i. Examples include:
  1. Partner with local museums and historical sites to develop an
  exhibit celebrating the cultural diversity located within the
  community, past and present.
   HEAR Commission 2023 Approved Annual Workplan
  May 23, 2023
  Page 4

  2. Partner with local agencies to facilitate the Commission’s
  programs including the Community Services and Historic
  Preservation & Cultural Resource Commissions, San Gabriel
  Police Department and the San Gabriel Unified School District.

7. Data Collection (Meets the Goals and Purpose of the Commission for Equity and
  Diversity)
  a. Gather information and analysis for traffic stops made by the San Gabriel
  Police Department and calls for suspicious people and vehicles made within
  2022.
